messages:
incident-bot: ⚠️ ALERT: continuous-batching path p99 latency spike detected for prod-region-us-west-2. p95: 180ms -> 420ms, p99: 520ms -> 3.2s. Streaming stalls observed for ~60s windows. Correlation: elevated mixed sequence-length variance.
maya: paging oncall — I'm on it. grabbing graphs now.
liam: saw this in dashboards, looks like a tail-of-tail from cont-batch scheduler delays. trying to reproduce locally.
oncall-rotations: @maya you are current oncall, handoff to you if needed.
ellie: adding context — a large customer ramped in that region ~ 06:10 UTC, requests with long prefix tokens increased. suspect mixed-seqlen bins causing unfair batching.
maya: confirmed spike aligns with 06:12 traffic bump. tracing to node i-0abc... GPU mem stable but queueing depth high.
ops-bot: rolling log snippet from node i-0abc: "WARN scheduler: batch_hold_time_exceeded=1800ms queue_len=23 mixed_seq_std=42"
liam: that queue_len is high. curious whether kv cache thrashing contributed. any evictions?
sara: kvcache evict rate jumped ~06:11 -> suggests long sequences evicting frequently.
ellie: customer impact: some streaming sessions reported stalls and partial responses. CS has 3 open cases, priority P2.
maya: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce max_batch_size on cont-batch to 8 (from 16), 2) enable per-seqlen fairness (experimental flag), 3) route streaming to dedicated low-latency pool (if capacity).
liam: prefer 1+3 short-term. reducing max_batch_size is quick; routing streaming off cont-batch needs config push.
maya: executing toggle now: updating featureflag contbatch.max_batch_size=8 for us-west-2. applying patch.
ops-bot: patch submitted: /api/flags/contbatch.max_batch_size set to 8 for us-west-2 by maya at 06:25 UTC. rollout 100%.
liam: monitoring p99...
maya: running a small one-off to force shedding: curl -X POST https://api.prod.redwood/v1/healthcheck -H 'x-rw-test: contbatch'
liam: p95 dropped to ~210ms, p99 trending down to 1.1s after ~60s. improvement but still above SLO (p99 target 800ms).
ellie: enabling per-seqlen fairness flag (experimental) in canary to see if scheduler picks smaller batches for long sequences.
maya: enabling per-seqlen fairness in canary pool now. /api/flags/contbatch.seqlen_fairness=on (canary only).
ops-bot: flag applied to canary pool nodes.
liam: can we preemptively evict large-KV entries for long-request customers? risk of quality drop but reduces memory churn.
sara: running kv eviction for heavy-customer 'acme-integration' on nodes i-0abc,i-0def. command: rwctl kvcache evict --customer acme-integration --confirm
ops-bot: kv eviction job queued, started at 06:34 UTC.
maya: still seeing intermittent streaming stalls — looks like scheduler fairness in canary reduced queueing but global pool still suffering.
liam: next mitigation: temporarily route streaming traffic to a 'streaming-fallback' model variant (smaller model, lower latency) for affected customers. requires route config change.
ellie: preparing route change for customers with open CS cases first. Sara, can you confirm which customers?
sara: acme, betaapps, syncly. confirmed.
maya: applying route override for those customers to streaming-fallback in us-west-2. /api/routes/override set.
ops-bot: route override applied for 3 customers.
liam: post-override p99 for those customers now ~680ms. global p99 improved to 850ms — still slightly above 800ms.
maya: filing incident page to summarize mitigation and next steps. tagging infra and runtime teams.
ellie: postmortem action items: - investigate scheduler binning threshold for mixed seq lengths - add auto-detect to lower batch sizes on seq-variance spikes - expand dedicated streaming pool capacity in us-west-2 - add KV cache pressure alert with preemption recommendations
liam: also add a quick rollback knob in console to route to fallback model per-customer.
sara: CS update sent to the 3 customers. response: acme acknowledged, prefers fallback until ops confirms stable.
oncall-rotations: maya — you started triage, would you like to hand off when you drop? next is liam.
maya: I'll stay until p99 < 800ms and stable for 15min, then handoff. current p99 = 790ms at 06:48 UTC.
liam: I'll pick up remaining infra investigations after handoff. please include notes about which flags we toggled and kv eviction job id.
maya: kv eviction job id: kv-evict-2026-06-12-0610. flags toggled: contbatch.max_batch_size->8, contbatch.seqlen_fairness->canary. route overrides applied for 3 customers.
ellie: creating follow-up board ticket INFRA-1432 for scheduler fixes and AUTO-BASED shedding.
maya: handoff -> liam at 07:05 UTC. leaving thread. :wave:
liam: acknowledged. continuing root cause analysis. will update with perf histogram and kernel-level traces.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity: S2 -> Reduced. Customer impact: degraded streaming for 3 customers, mitigations applied.
sara: thanks all. will update CS thread.
liam: next steps: collect scheduler traces, evaluate per-seqlen fairness rollout to all pools, run load test with mixed seq distribution. aiming for full resolution ticket by EOD.
ops-bot: Incident closed for paging at 07:20 UTC (alert suppressed). Further investigation continues in INFRA-1432.
liam: fyi - added repro script in /runbooks/contbatch/mixed-seqlen-repro.sh and will link perf graphs in the ticket.
maya: thanks team.
